_comment: Every credential shape this project or its upstreams issue, in one place.
See doc.go for why this is data and not Go source, and for the rules a new
`example` and `counterexample` are written as PARTS and joined by whoever
reads this file. A whole example would be a literal credential shape sitting
in the tree, which is the one thing the list exists to forbid — and the tree
scan reads this file like any other.

shapes.name: anthropic-api-key
shapes.why: Anthropic issues these to whoever pays for the model calls; the prefix is fixed.

shapes.name: openai-project-key
shapes.why: The project-scoped form OpenAI issues from its dashboard.

shapes.name: openai-api-key
shapes.why: The older unscoped form, and the shape every OpenAI-compatible endpoint copied.

shapes.name: assigned-api-key
shapes.why: Not a vendor's shape but a syntax: a long opaque value assigned to a field called api_key. It is how a key arrives in a YAML manifest or an env file whatever issued it.

shapes.name: kaimahi-credential
shapes.why: This plane's own. It belongs in a Secret the Agent REFERENCES, never in the Agent, a blueprint, or any file in this repository — including a test fixture, which is why the fixtures that need one assemble it at run time.

shapes.name: github-token
shapes.why: The classic prefixes: ghp_ personal, gho_/ghu_ the OAuth and user-to-server tokens a Copilot device-flow login mints, ghs_ a server token, ghr_ a refresh token.

shapes.name: github-fine-grained-token
shapes.why: The repository-scoped form, which is what this project's own GitHub seams ask an operator for.

shapes.name: slack-token
shapes.why: Bot, user, app-configuration and refresh tokens. The Slack seam is the one this repository has run live, so this is the shape most likely to arrive in a pasted transcript.

shapes.name: slack-app-token
shapes.why: Socket Mode's own token, which is NOT an xox shape and so was missed by every list that only knew about xoxb.

shapes.name: azure-devops-pat
shapes.what: an Azure DevOps personal access token
shapes.why: Azure DevOps issues a bare 52-character base32 value with no prefix at all, so this is a shape rule and nothing more: a 52-character run of lowercase letters and the digits 2 to 7, whole-word. It is the loosest rule in this list and the only one that could in principle fire on something that is not a credential; a real hex digest carries 0, 1, 8 or 9 and a base64 value carries uppercase or +/=, so neither matches.

shapes.name: json-web-token
shapes.why: The Entra access token an ADO or Azure seam refreshes into, and any other bearer JWT. Its header always begins with the base64 of {"alg", which is eyJ.

shapes.name: private-key
shapes.why: A PEM header. No upstream here issues one, which is exactly why a file carrying it is a mistake rather than a design.
